item.description: • No more early traffic lights in Mission Control. After you close a window, the lights wait until the next window has finished sliding under the pointer.

• Unsaved changes aren't left hidden. If a window you close (or an app you quit) asks "Save changes?", Mission Plus now leaves the overview or Mission Control and brings that window forward so you can answer. Before, the question waited out of sight behind the overview.

• Smoother Mission Control again. After you close or minimize a window, Mission Control rearranges the rest as smoothly as before. 1.1.0 queried macOS about Spaces dozens of times a second while Mission Control was open, which competed with its animation.
  • ⌘W and ⌘M in Mission Control respond faster.

• Windows from every Space, if you want them. In Preferences, the overview can also show windows on other desktops, full-screen windows, minimized windows and windows of hidden apps, in a strip along the bottom. F, M and H mark full-screen, minimized and hidden ones. Opening one switches to its Space, restores it or unhides its app.
  • Tidy up without leaving. ⌘H, ⌘Q, ⌘W and ⌘M no longer close the overview. With hidden or minimized windows shown, ⌘H and ⌘M move windows into the strip, and pressing them again undoes it.
  • Straight to the window you pick, even when its app has windows on several Spaces.
  • Sharper exit. The window you open grows from a full-resolution snapshot.
  • Windows without a thumbnail show their app's icon and title on a tint of the app's colours.
  • Fixed: in Mission Control, close and minimize buttons could appear over windows from other Spaces.

First public release.

  • Close and minimize buttons in Mission Control. Hover any window in macOS's own Mission Control to get traffic-light buttons on it.
  • Keyboard shortcuts in Mission Control. ⌘W, ⌘M, ⌘H and ⌘Q act on the highlighted window; ⌥⌘W and ⌥⌘M close or minimize everything; ⌥⌘H hides every other app; arrow keys move between windows and ↵ opens one.
  • Window Overview. A Mission Control–style overview of every window, with live thumbnails and type-to-search. Open it with ⌃⌥↑ (or your own shortcut), or let it replace the three- or four-finger swipe up.
  • Updates. Mission Plus checks for new versions once a day and asks before installing.
